back: The part of a computer that processes the instructions and data input into it so that results can be output or stored.
A CPU made as an integrated circuit on a single chip.
Carries out arithmetic (calculations) and logical operations (comparisons, AND, OR, NOT).
Decodes instructions and sends control signals to co-ordinate the other parts of the computer.
Memory (mainly RAM) holding the programs and data currently in use, directly accessed by the CPU.
Fetch an instruction from main memory → decode it → execute it, billions of times a second.
The case is the system unit; the CPU is the processor chip on the motherboard inside it.

front: Why programs are loaded into RAM
back: The CPU can only directly access main memory, so programs are copied from secondary storage into RAM to run.
Arithmetic logic unit, control unit and main memory.
